questions.question: In story S5 (Handlers: poll, profile, profile-request, announcement and retract coverage), is there any vacuous or placeholder production path: a no-op/stub body, a tautological assertion, a frozen stand-in constant, or an optional dependency (injected port, handler, client handle) that silently degrades to non-behavior when not injected? Cite file:line for each injection point in app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/pollHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/profileHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/profileRequestHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/leaveHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/announcementFamily.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/pollPersistence.ts and show that omitting the dependency fails loudly rather than succeeding silently.

Could `handlers` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md (imports only via each module's index.ts, no React-context imports under app/src/lib/marmot/**, no ts-mls or @internet-privacy/marmot-ts imports)?

Does S5 comply with the architecture.md boundary rules: only `client/` constructs or disposes the MarmotClient, code inside HistoryBackend calls / inbox handlers / client listeners never awaits an account-scope client call (follow-up work via the owned setTimeout(0) FIFO), group sender identity comes only from orderingKey.account, and idb-keyval update() is not used? List each rule touched by this story's files with file:line evidence, or state why it is not touched.

Do unit, property, and (where the AC names them) library-harness or e2e tests cover the artifacts named in S5's scope (app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/pollHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/profileHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/profileRequestHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/handlers/leaveHandler.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/announcementFamily.ts; app/src/lib/marmot/pollPersistence.ts)? Show that tests use real collaborators or test fixtures rather than mocking the helper used at the SUT call site, that idb mocks are seeded out of key order where order matters, and that at least one test fails if the production code is replaced by a no-op.

Does the delivered S5 implementation match the intent of its scope (Re-point poll, profile, profile-request, announcement (+ leave-announcement) handlers to the new signature, live-accessor roster/admin gates (group.members()/group.admins), unregistered-kind pass-through, retract for every kind (other members' content removed and unread recomputed; own chat to faile) and respect its exclusions (Chat/reaction/delete-edit (S4))? Identify any capability owned by a later story that was built ahead, or any in-scope capability left unimplemented.

Which trust or validation boundaries does S5 touch (signer budget/permissions, relay-supplied events, rumor sender/pubkey attribution, invite/join payloads, privacy invariant that no profile metadata is published to public relays)? Show the validation or defensive check at each boundary with file:line evidence and a test that feeds a malformed or hostile input and observes rejection.

AC-HIST-9: Handlers for chat (kind 9), reaction (7), delete (5), edit (10/11/12 as registered), poll (as registered), profile (0), profile-request (30) and announcement rumors MUST each be reachable from `append` via the rumor kind; an unregistered kind MUST be stored and marked `dispatched:true` with no handler call and no throw. Asserted per kind with a stub store: the corresponding store receives the row. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-HIST-11: Roster and admin gates inside handlers (announcement roster gate, profile-request gate, admin-only signals) MUST read live `group.members()` / `group.admins` accessors, never the overlay. A test where overlay and live accessor disagree MUST gate by the live accessor. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-HIST-12: The existing behavioural handler suites (chat, reactions, delete/edit, polls, profile, profile-request, announcement roster gate) MUST be re-pointed at the new handler signature `{groupId, eventId, rumor, sender}` and pass; `handlersRumorPubkeyBoundary` MUST be re-expressed asserting that a handler given `sender ≠ rumor.pubkey` attributes the content to `sender`. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-WDR-1: After `withdraw` of an entry authored by another member, that member's chat row, reaction and poll event MUST be absent from the stores, and the group's unread count MUST equal the value recomputed over the remaining rows (asserted with a concrete before/after count). Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.

AC-WDR-2: An own chat row that was withdrawn MUST end in the existing failed/retry status (not deleted) and MUST NOT be auto-resent (send spy call count unchanged). Own withdrawn reactions, votes, edit and delete signals MUST be dropped from the stores. Provide evidence of (a) the production code satisfying this (file:line), (b) the test(s) at level [unit] that exercise it end-to-end and would fail for a stub/no-op, and (c) confirmation that those tests are not pure mock-spy proxies.
